title: Halve Evens, Decrement Odds
statement:
You start with a whole number num. While it is not zero, take one step: if the number is even, divide it by 2; if it is odd, subtract 1.

Return how many steps it takes to reach 0. Starting at 0 takes no steps.

examples.why: 13 → 12 → 6 → 3 → 2 → 1 → 0. Odd numbers cost an extra step before they can be halved.
16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 → 0. A power of two only ever halves, plus one final subtraction.

hints: Just follow the rules in a loop first. How many times can the loop run for a number up to a million?
Look at the number in binary. What does halving do to the bits? What does subtracting 1 from an odd number do?
Halving drops the last bit; subtracting 1 from an odd number clears a trailing 1. So every 1-bit costs one subtraction and every bit except the top costs one halving.

explain.intuition:
Write the number in binary. Dividing an even number by 2 is a right shift: the last bit (a 0) falls off. Subtracting 1 from an odd number turns its last bit from 1 to 0 and changes nothing else.

So each 1-bit costs exactly one subtraction, and every bit position except the highest one costs one shift. The answer is (number of bits − 1) + (number of 1-bits) for any num > 0. For 13 = 1101 that is 3 + 3 = 6.
steps: Loop while num > 0: if the lowest bit is 1, count one step for the subtraction.
If num > 1, count one more step for the shift, then shift right by one.
When num is 1, its subtraction was counted and no shift is needed, so stop.
pitfalls: Counting a shift for the top bit too. After the last subtraction the number is 0, not something to halve, so the formula has bits − 1 shifts.
Forgetting num = 0: the formula would give −1 because 0 has no bits.

solutions.title: Follow the rules
solutions.idea: Simulate: halve when even, subtract when odd, count steps. The number at least halves every two steps, so the loop is short.

solutions.title: Count bits
solutions.idea: Every 1-bit costs one subtraction and every bit below the top one costs one halving.

followups: Now the odd rule may also add 1 instead of subtracting 1. What is the fewest number of steps?
The input is a binary string with a million digits. How do you answer without converting it to a number?
